title: Finite-evaluation primitive operator for any finite-index coset rectangle
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a profinite group $G$ (a compact Hausdorff topological group with a basis of open normal subgroups), an open subgroup $H\subseteq G$ of finite index $m=[G:H]$, an integer $n\geq1$, and elements $a_0,\ldots,a_n\in G$. Use $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and the universes of [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], [def-weil-size-convention]. For any normed $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector space $V$ whose norm satisfies $\|v+w\|\leq\max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$ and $\|av\|=|a|_\ell\|v\|$, put $C^r(G,V)=C(G^r,V)$ with the norm topology on $V$, trivial $G$-action, $C^0(G,V)=V$, $d^0=0$, and
$$(dc)(g_1,\ldots,g_{r+1})=c(g_2,\ldots,g_{r+1})+\sum_{i=1}^r(-1)^ic(g_1,\ldots,g_i g_{i+1},\ldots,g_{r+1})+(-1)^{r+1}c(g_1,\ldots,g_r).$$
There is a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear operator $T:C^n(G,V)\to C^{n-1}(G,V)$ of the form
$$(Tc)(x)=\sum_{k=1}^u\alpha_k c(\psi_k(x)),$$
where $u$ is finite, $\psi_k:G^{n-1}\to G^n$ is continuous and $\alpha_k\in\mathbf Q_\ell$ satisfies $|\alpha_k|_\ell\leq |m|_\ell^{-1}$. The choices depend only on $G,H,n,(a_i)$, not on $V$. Whenever $dc=0$ and the homogeneous function
$$f_c(g_0,\ldots,g_n)=c(g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1}^{-1}g_n)$$
vanishes on $Ha_0\times\cdots\times Ha_n$, one has $d(Tc)=c$. The same formulas, leaving a profinite parameter $s\in S$ fixed, define continuous operators on $C(S\times G^n,V)$ and have supremum-norm bound $|m|_\ell^{-1}$. They preserve every $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear coefficient subspace. No prime-to-$\ell$ condition on $m$ and no completeness of $V$ is assumed.

Ordered-join chain comparison followed by averaging over finitely many cosets, allowing the bound |[G:H]|_ell^(-1). WANTED: an exact continuous-cochain reference; the blueprint does not assert this auxiliary lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-topological-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates] with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, $J=G$, and trivial action on $V$. The norm assumptions make addition, negation and scalar multiplication continuous: addition obeys the maximum estimate, and near $(a_0,v_0)$ the difference $av-a_0v_0=a(v-v_0)+(a-a_0)v_0$ has norm at most $\max(|a|_\ell\|v-v_0\|,|a-a_0|_\ell\|v_0\|)$, with $|a|_\ell$ locally bounded. Write $\Psi c=f_c$ and $\Phi F(g_1,\ldots,g_q)=F(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_q)$. The cited statement gives inverse linear cochain maps, $\delta\Psi=\Psi d$ and $\Phi\delta=d\Phi$, including degree zero. Consequently $dc=0$ implies $\delta f_c=0$. No completeness of $V$ is used.

proof.text: Choose a transversal $D\subset G$ for the finitely many right cosets $H\backslash G$, including $1$. Write $x=\rho(x)s(x)$ uniquely with $\rho(x)\in H$ and $s(x)\in D$. Each coset $Hs$ is clopen: it is open by translation, and its complement is a union of other open cosets. On $Hs$, $\rho(x)=xs^{-1}$ is continuous into $H$ with its subspace topology; these open pieces show that $\rho:G\to H$ is continuous. Uniqueness gives $\rho(hx)=h\rho(x)$ for $h\in H$. The transversal is fixed once, independently of $V$. No normality of $H$ is assumed.

proof.text: For a set $Y$ let $B_q(Y)$ be the free abelian group with specified basis $[y_0,\ldots,y_q]$ (repetitions allowed), and put $B_{-1}(Y)=\mathbf Z[\varnothing]$. This is the basis convention of [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Define $\partial$ by alternating deletion, including $\partial[y]=[\varnothing]$ and $\partial[\varnothing]=0$. Deleting two distinct positions in opposite orders gives opposite signs, hence $\partial^2=0$. A homogeneous function $F$ extends uniquely by finite sums to $\widehat F:B_n(G)\to V$; then $\delta F=0$ means $\widehat F\partial=0$ on $B_{n+1}(G)$. Left translation acts coordinatewise on all these chains.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ordered-join-partial-contraction] with $r=n+1$ and the separately labelled sets $X_i=Ha_i$. Write $J_q$ for its ordered-color chains and $e_q:J_q\to B_q(G)$ for erasing colors; $\partial e=e\partial$ follows from deletion. For $h\in H$, choose anchors $v_i=ha_i$ and denote the cited operator by $S^h$. Its statement gives $\partial S^h_q+S^h_{q-1}\partial=1$ for $-1\leq q\leq n-1$, its naturality under simultaneous left translation, and a fixed finite integer expansion using only vertex insertions and replacements. In degree $n$, every basis of $J_n$ has exactly one vertex in each color, in order $0,\ldots,n$; thus every tuple in $e_n(J_n)$ is an integer combination of tuples in the specified rectangle.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written finite-index rectangle primitive construction, step 4; this cochain argument is not asserted in the blueprint. Stacks Tag 0DVG (etale-cohomology-section-continuous-group-cohomology) fixes the cochain convention.

proof.text:
Construct $P_q:B_q(G)\to J_q$ through degree $n$. Put $P_{-1}=1$ and $P_0[x]=[(0,\rho(x)a_0)]$, so $\partial P_0=P_{-1}\partial$. For $1\leq q\leq n$, assuming the chain identities below degree $q$, define on each basis tuple $x=[x_0,\ldots,x_q]$
$$z=P_{q-1}(\partial x),\qquad P_q(x)=S^{\rho(x_0)}_{q-1}(z),$$
and extend linearly. The induction hypothesis gives $\partial z=P_{q-2}\partial^2x=0$, using the augmentation identity when $q=1$. Since $q-1\leq n-1$, [lem-sfb-ordered-join-partial-contraction] gives $\partial P_q(x)=z$. Hence $\partial P_q=P_{q-1}\partial$ in all required degrees. The input-dependent anchor is chosen on basis tuples before linear extension; it is not asserted to be a linear function of a general chain.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written finite-index rectangle primitive construction, step 5; this cochain argument is not asserted in the blueprint. Stacks Tag 0DVG (etale-cohomology-section-continuous-group-cohomology) fixes the cochain convention.

proof.text: Naturality in [lem-sfb-ordered-join-partial-contraction], applied to left translation by $h\in H$, gives $hS^{\rho(x_0)}z=S^{h\rho(x_0)}(hz)$. Together with $\rho(hx_0)=h\rho(x_0)$ this proves inductively $P_q(hx)=hP_q(x)$; the base case is the displayed $P_0$. The finite-expansion clause of that node also proves inductively that $P_q[x_0,\ldots,x_q]$ is a fixed finite integer sum of colored tuples with vertices of the form $\rho(x_j)a_i$. Boundary merely selects subtuples, and the next $S$ inserts or replaces by $\rho(x_0)a_i$. Coefficient lists and coordinate selections depend on the degree and color lists alone. Keep repeated terms rather than combining them, so no equality test on input values enters this expansion.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written finite-index rectangle primitive construction, step 6; this cochain argument is not asserted in the blueprint. Stacks Tag 0DVG (etale-cohomology-section-continuous-group-cohomology) fixes the cochain convention.

proof.text:
Set $A_q=e_qP_q$ for $-1\leq q\leq n$. These are $H$-equivariant augmented chain maps and $A_{-1}=1$. For $b\in G$, let $C_b$ prefix $b$ to a tuple, with $C_b[\varnothing]=[b]$. Direct deletion gives
$$\partial[b,y_0,\ldots,y_q]=[y_0,\ldots,y_q]-C_b\partial[y_0,\ldots,y_q],$$
so $\partial C_b+C_b\partial=1$, also in degree $-1$ since $\partial[b]=[\varnothing]$. Coordinatewise translation gives $hC_bz=C_{hb}(hz)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written finite-index rectangle primitive construction, step 7; this cochain argument is not asserted in the blueprint. Stacks Tag 0DVG (etale-cohomology-section-continuous-group-cohomology) fixes the cochain convention.

proof.text:
Define $Q_{-1}=0$ and, on basis tuples $x=[x_0,\ldots,x_q]$, recursively for $0\leq q\leq n$ put
$$Z_q(x)=x-A_qx-Q_{q-1}\partial x,\qquad Q_q(x)=C_{x_0}Z_q(x),$$
extending linearly. The augmentation of $Z_0$ is $1-1=0$. For $q\geq1$, the previous-degree identity and the chain identity for $A$ give
$$\partial Z_q=(1-A_{q-1})\partial x-(1-A_{q-1}-Q_{q-2}\partial)\partial x=0.$$
The prefix identity therefore gives $\partial Q_q(x)=Z_q(x)$. This proves by induction
$$1-A_q=\partial Q_q+Q_{q-1}\partial\qquad(0\leq q\leq n).$$
Both the base and the step have been verified, rather than invoking an unspecified resolution-comparison theorem.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written finite-index rectangle primitive construction, step 8; this cochain argument is not asserted in the blueprint. Stacks Tag 0DVG (etale-cohomology-section-continuous-group-cohomology) fixes the cochain convention.

proof.text: Induction in this same recursion proves $H$-equivariance of $Q$: $Z_q(hx)=hZ_q(x)$ and $C_{hx_0}(hZ_q(x))=hQ_q(x)$. Its base is $Q_{-1}=0$. Likewise the finite expansion for $A$, together with deletion, subtraction and prefixing, proves that each $Q_q[x_0,\ldots,x_q]$ has a fixed finite integer expansion with every vertex either $x_j$ or $\rho(x_j)a_i$. These vertex maps are continuous by step 2 and multiplication in $G$. Thus evaluation of any continuous $F$ on $Q_q$ or $A_q$ is continuous. All the recursions are integral and independent of coefficients.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written finite-index rectangle primitive construction, step 9; this cochain argument is not asserted in the blueprint. Stacks Tag 0DVG (etale-cohomology-section-continuous-group-cohomology) fixes the cochain convention.

proof.text:
For a continuous diagonally $G$-invariant homogeneous function $F:G^{n+1}\to V$, define a function on $G^n$ by
$$(UF)(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})=\widehat F(Q_{n-1}[x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}]).$$
The finite formulas in step 9 show that $UF$ is continuous and linear in $F$, and $H$-equivariance of $Q$ and invariance of $F$ show $UF(hx)=UF(x)$ for $h\in H$. If $\delta F=0$ and $F$ vanishes on $Ha_0\times\cdots\times Ha_n$, then $\widehat F A_n=0$, since every term of $A_n$ is an ordered rectangle tuple by step 4. Apply $\widehat F$ to $1-A_n=\partial Q_n+Q_{n-1}\partial$ from step 8. The term $\widehat F\partial Q_n$ is zero by the cocycle identity, and the other term is precisely $\delta(UF)$. Thus $F=\delta(UF)$ as functions on all of $G^{n+1}$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written finite-index rectangle primitive construction, step 10; this cochain argument is not asserted in the blueprint. Stacks Tag 0DVG (etale-cohomology-section-continuous-group-cohomology) fixes the cochain convention.

proof.text:
For an $H$-invariant homogeneous function $L:G^{q+1}\to V$, put
$$(\mathcal M_qL)(x_0,\ldots,x_q)=m^{-1}\sum_{s\in D}L(sx_0,\ldots,sx_q).$$
Here $m\geq1$, and it is invertible in $\mathbf Q_\ell$ since that field has characteristic zero [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. For $g\in G$, write $sg=hu$ with $h\in H$, $u\in D$. Right multiplication by $g$ permutes the right cosets $H\backslash G$, so $s\mapsto u$ is a permutation and $L(sgx)=L(hux)=L(ux)$. It follows that $\mathcal M_qL$ is $G$-invariant. Deleting a coordinate commutes with simultaneous left translation, hence $\delta\mathcal M_q=\mathcal M_{q+1}\delta$. If $F$ is $G$-invariant, each summand equals $F$ and $\mathcal M_qF=m^{-1}mF=F$. Therefore step 10 implies $F=\delta(\mathcal M_{n-1}UF)$ for the specified rectangle-vanishing cocycles. Finite addition preserves continuity and linearity. This argument requires neither normality of $H$ nor a prime-to-$\ell$ index.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written finite-index rectangle primitive construction, step 11; this cochain argument is not asserted in the blueprint. Stacks Tag 0DVG (etale-cohomology-section-continuous-group-cohomology) fixes the cochain convention.

proof.text:
Define on every continuous inhomogeneous $n$-cochain, without any cocycle or vanishing assumption,
$$T=\Phi_{n-1}\mathcal M_{n-1}U\Psi_n.$$
Its output is a continuous $(n-1)$-cochain because $\mathcal M U\Psi c$ is a continuous $G$-invariant homogeneous function. It is $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear. For a cocycle $c$ vanishing homogeneously on the rectangle, step 11 and [lem-sfb-topological-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates] give
$$dTc=\Phi_n\delta\mathcal M_{n-1}U\Psi_nc=\Phi_n\Psi_nc=c.$$
To obtain its finite evaluation formula, expand $Q_{n-1}$ by step 9, translate each resulting tuple by each $s\in D$, and substitute the cumulative-product tuple $(1,x_1,x_1x_2,\ldots,x_1\cdots x_{n-1})$ from $\Phi$. Finally replace every homogeneous tuple $(b_0,\ldots,b_n)$ by $(b_0^{-1}b_1,\ldots,b_{n-1}^{-1}b_n)$ from $\Psi$. All these coordinate maps are continuous, so their composites are maps $\psi_k:G^{n-1}\to G^n$. All coefficients are integers divided by $m$. The formulas were fixed by the transversal and integral chain recursions, independently of $V$; repeated terms may be left uncollected.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written finite-index rectangle primitive construction, step 12; this cochain argument is not asserted in the blueprint. Stacks Tag 0DVG (etale-cohomology-section-continuous-group-cohomology) fixes the cochain convention.

proof.text: For each integer $k$, the definition of the $\ell$-adic valuation in [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] gives $|k|_\ell\leq1$, and multiplicativity gives $|k/m|_\ell\leq |m|_\ell^{-1}$. This proves the requested coefficient bound even when $\ell$ divides $m$. If $\|c(z)\|\leq B$ for every $z\in G^n$, the finite-sum ultrametric inequality gives $\|(Tc)(x)\|\leq |m|_\ell^{-1}B$ for every $x$. Taking supremum norms yields $\|Tc\|_\infty\leq |m|_\ell^{-1}\|c\|_\infty$. A continuous cochain on the compact domain $G^n$ has bounded norm, so these are finite suprema. Every output value is a finite $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear combination of input values. Thus the operator preserves any linear coefficient subspace, with no closedness requirement and no passage to a limit in $V$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written finite-index rectangle primitive construction, step 13; this cochain argument is not asserted in the blueprint. Stacks Tag 0DVG (etale-cohomology-section-continuous-group-cohomology) fixes the cochain convention.

proof.text:
Let $S$ be profinite. For $c\in C(S\times G^n,V)$ set
$$(Tc)(s,x)=\sum_k\alpha_k c(s,\psi_k(x)).$$
The maps $(s,x)\mapsto(s,\psi_k(x))$ are continuous, and finite addition and fixed scalar multiplication in $V$ are continuous, so the resulting family is continuous. The estimate of step 13 applies uniformly in both variables and proves the same supremum bound on the parameter family. Cochain identities and rectangle vanishing are evaluated at each fixed $s$, and the subspace assertion again follows from the finite linear formula. If $S$ is empty the assertion holds for the unique family. For $n=1$, $Q_0[x]=[x,x]-[x,\rho(x)a_0]$, and after averaging $\mathcal M_0UF$ is a $G$-invariant function on $G$, hence constant. Its homogeneous differential is zero, agreeing with $d^0=0$. The degree-$1$ identity in step 10 therefore also shows that any such rectangle-vanishing $1$-cocycle is zero. Zero coefficient spaces and incomplete normed spaces are covered by the same finite formulas.
